ai.title: Fix newline on paste in CLI
ai.summary: Prevents readline from triggering execution when pasting previous commands in npm-app/src/cli.ts. Replaces direct rl.write with cursor movement hack and internal line refresh.

eli5.text: When you paste a previous command in the terminal tool, it no longer accidentally runs right away. Previously, the system would send your pasted text including a press of the Enter key, which triggered the command to execute unexpectedly. Now, it inserts the text without the Enter, so you can review or edit it before choosing to run it.

ai.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro added to max cost mode
ai.summary: Backend routes 'max' cost mode requests to new streamGemini25Pro function, replacing Claude default. Implements fallback chain: OpenRouter stream -> Gemini API stream -> Vertex AI stream. Updates main-prompt.ts to conditionally select model based on costMode. Adds debug-subset.log to .gitignore and renames OpenRouter stream functions for clarity.

eli5.text: Starting today, people using the premium "max" option to spend more for better results will now get conversations powered by Google's Gemini 2.5 Pro model instead of the old default. When you type a message in max mode, your request goes to a new streaming path that tries Google's service first, and if that doesn't work, it can still fall back to the older providers. You won't see a setting to turn on or off: the model choice happens automatically based on which plan tier you're on.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.199
ai.summary: Bump `npm-app/package.json` version from 1.0.198 to 1.0.199. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: The assistant's packaging label ticked up one small step, but the thing you'd actually care about is that the most expensive "go all out" mode now talks to a newer, stronger model behind the scenes instead of the usual one. That's the part you'd notice if you kicked off a request on the priciest setting today, since it now reaches for that updated model by default. Everything else in this batch is quieter cleanup and internal housekeeping that you won't see directly.

ai.title: Fix main-prompt test assertions
ai.summary: Rewrote `backend/src/__tests__/main-prompt.test.ts` to strictly verify message history order. Replaced loose `find` checks with explicit index assertions for tool results, instructions, prompt, and assistant messages. Updated prompt content validation to expect array structures with text blocks.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team rewrote the test that checks the order of messages in a conversation, replacing loose searches with strict position checks and updating how prompt content is validated to expect structured text blocks. Nothing changes for you directly since this only affects internal testing, but you might notice if you looked at the test results: they now verify that messages appear in a specific sequence (tool results, instructions, prompt, then assistant reply) and that prompt content follows a consistent format. This is part of ongoing stability maintenance to catch future regressions in how conversation history is built.

ai.title: Type fixes in main-prompt test
ai.summary: Updated `backend/src/__tests__/main-prompt.test.ts` to satisfy TypeScript strict checks. Added explicit `as any` casts for `content` array access and reformatted long variable assignments to prevent linting errors. Scope limited to backend test suite.

eli5.text: This is a small, behind-the-scenes fix to the assistant's internal testing files. Engineers cleaned up some formatting and added explicit type instructions so the tests run under stricter quality checks. You, as a user, would see nothing different, it's housekeeping that keeps the system's self-checks from failing. No features changed and no one is affected by it.

ai.title: Joker emoji added to CLI greeting
ai.summary: Appends a 🃏 emoji to the `displayGreeting` output string in `npm-app/src/menu.ts`. This is a cosmetic update to the CLI welcome message.

eli5.text: The next time you open the command-line tool and see the welcome message, you'll notice a playing-card joker emoji (🃏) tacked onto the end of the greeting line. Nothing else about the message changed; it still welcomes you by name if you have one. You would only spot it if you were looking at the text that scrolls by when the tool starts up. The change is already live for anyone using the tool today.

ai.title: Fix null character stripping in message cost tracker
ai.summary: Refactored `saveMessage` in `backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts` to use a new recursive utility `stripNullCharsFromObject` from `backend/src/util/object.ts`. Previously, null characters were stripped from the `request` field by serializing and deserializing the entire object via JSON, which could fail or be inefficient. The new utility traverses objects and arrays, applying `stripNullChars` directly to string values. This ensures robust cleaning of request and response payloads before database insertion without relying on JSON round-trips.

eli5.text: If you send messages that contain special invisible characters called null characters, the system now cleans them out properly before storing them. The system used to remove these characters by converting messages to a simplified format and back, which sometimes broke or slowed things down. Now it uses a smarter method that goes through the whole message and removes those characters safely and quickly, so your messages get stored correctly no matter what's inside them.

ai.title: Refactor LRU cache to native Map
ai.summary: LRUCache in common/src/util/lru-cache.ts now relies on native Map insertion order instead of a custom MinHeap for eviction tracking. The get method deletes and re-sets keys to mark them as recently used, while set evicts the first key from the Map's iterator when capacity is exceeded. This removes dependency on common/src/util/min-heap.ts for cache logic, though the heap class remains in the codebase with minor variable renaming. Constructor validation throws an error if maxSize is not positive.

eli5.text: If you use the assistant and your session includes the cache, you might not notice a thing, that's the point. The team swapped out the behind-the-scenes system the assistant uses to remember recent responses for a simpler one built into the tool itself, so the assistant still recalls what you just said without any visible change in speed or behavior. This is live today and only affects how the assistant manages its short-term memory internally.

ai.title: Enforce unique fingerprints and update auth logic
ai.summary: CLI fingerprints now append 8 random bytes to ensure uniqueness across identical hardware, preventing session collisions. Auth flow updates include removing fingerprint auto-insertion from `/api/auth/cli/code`, adding `expiresAt` to response payloads, and resetting `sig_hash` on logout. Backend WebSocket logging context drops `authToken` to reduce sensitive data exposure. Changes span `npm-app/src/fingerprint.ts`, `web/src/app/api/auth/cli/*`, and `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts`.

eli5.text: When you sign in with the command-line tool on more than one computer, each tool now gets a slightly different identity tag. Previously, two identical machines could end up with the same tag, causing their login sessions to mix up or overwrite each other; now the tool adds a small random value to the tag so every machine is uniquely recognized. If you looked at the login process, you would also notice that the tool no longer automatically creates this identity tag for you when requesting a code, that login responses now include when they expire, and that logging out clears the stored signature so it cannot be reused. The system also stopped writing your access token into debug logs when sending prompts or connecting, so less sensitive information is recorded while you work.

When you run the assistant CLI, its welcome greeting now ends with a joker face emoji after the text it already displayed. That is a packaging label change; the visible new behavior is simply the added emoji in the greeting.

ai.title: Add pagination and fix overage stats in analyze-overages script
ai.summary: Updated `scripts/analyze-overages.ts` to fetch active subscriptions using pagination instead of a single limit-100 call. Fixed subscription null check and corrected overage statistics calculations to filter for actual overages, use proper cents-to-dollars conversion, and distinguish between established customers and those with overages.

eli5.text: The tool the team uses to check who is paying extra usage fees now checks every single active subscriber instead of stopping at the first 100. That means anyone past that first batch who went over their plan limit will now show up in the report. The numbers it prints are also corrected so the totals only count people who actually had overage charges, and the average is figured from just those people instead of dividing by everyone on the plan. No dates or regions in the evidence, so if it landed on 2025-04-01 it is on internal tooling, not customer-facing billing.

ai.title: Clarify tool call XML formatting in backend prompt
ai.summary: Refined system prompt instructions in `backend/src/tools.ts` to explicitly forbid wrapping raw tool call XML in markdown code blocks. Added concrete negative and positive examples to prevent parsing errors caused by ```xml fences. This internal change targets prompt adherence to ensure correct tool execution.

eli5.text: The system now receives clearer instructions telling it not to put tool commands inside special formatting boxes, which was causing those commands to get misread. If you looked, you'd see the example instructions show both the wrong way and the right way to write things out, without any fancy wrapping. This affects how the system internally formats its own tool usage but doesn't change any features you'd see day to day.
